messages:
amelia: Heads-up — we just saw ALB in us-west-2 start deregistering ~10 pods from edge-pool-2 with 'unhealthy' health checks around 09:18 UTC. No deploys. CloudWatch shows lots of TCP RSTs on health-check ports.
raj: ugh, same cluster? any recent node kernel / kube-proxy changes?
amelia: nope, last deploy 12h ago. nodes are 1.26.1. I'm ssh'ing into one node to curl the pod IP from localhost.
amelia: `curl -v --connect-timeout 1 http://10.44.12.7:8080/healthz` -> hangs then connection reset.
simon: can you check conntrack table counts? `sudo conntrack -S | grep entries`
amelia: running now: `entries: 98120` — node has nf_conntrack_max=100000 by default.
raj: that looks tight. If nodes are SNATing healthchecks (externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster) ALB -> node -> pod will consume ephemeral ports on node for each check; with many checks we can exhaust ephemeral ports/conntrack and start RSTs.
infra-bot: deploy-bot noticed increased ALB healthcheck failures for target-group tg-0a1b2c in us-west-2 at 2026-03-18T09:18:35Z.
ops-oncall: Can we confirm service type and k8s Service.externalTrafficPolicy?
amelia: svc/edge-svc is type: LoadBalancer, externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster. TargetGroup is ALB (targetType=instance).
raj: that matches SNAT path. Two mitigations: set externalTrafficPolicy: Local (avoid SNAT for node-local endpoints) OR switch ALB target group to targetType=ip so ALB talks directly to PodIPs (if allowed). Also bump conntrack max as short-term.
simon: quick repro: run `for i in {1..20000}; do curl -sS --connect-timeout 1 http://$NODE_IP:31000/healthz >/dev/null || echo fail; done` and watch `conntrack -S`.
amelia: tried scaling traffic simulation — conntrack climbed to 110k and kernel started dropping entries, then health checks started failing.
ops-oncall: I'll push a temporary sysctl change across the ASG: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` and apply via DaemonSet to make durable.
amelia: thanks. Also let's change svc to externalTrafficPolicy: Local on edge-svc and update ALB target group later. Planning a short maintenance window?
raj: ExternalTrafficPolicy: Local means ALB health checks will only hit nodes with endpoints. Need to ensure we have nodePort on those nodes and not break cross-az routing. Also ensure readinessProbe is tight (shorter timeout) so we don't send checks to pods still starting.
ops-oncall: rolling the sysctl now. Monitoring CloudWatch for reduced RSTs.
infra-bot: sysctl update applied to 6 nodes in asg-edge-west-2.
amelia: within 120s health check failures dropped from ~60/min to ~2/min. ALB stopped deregistering targets.
simon: followups: 1) plan to migrate to targetType=ip for new target groups to avoid node SNAT in long term; 2) set externalTrafficPolicy: Local for edge-svc after verifying AZ distribution; 3) add conntrack autosize/alert for >70% usage; 4) document in runbook.
raj: add a short note about pod termination/graceful shutdown — with externalTrafficPolicy Local we need to make sure kube-proxy/iptables doesn't send traffic to terminating pods (but readiness handles that).
ops-oncall: I'll open a PR for the k8s svc change + annotation for ALB target type, and add sysctl DaemonSet as fallback.
amelia: PR #472 opened with svc patch and rollout plan. I'll coordinate the maintenance and smoke tests.
simon: thanks team. closing for now, will add postmortem if something regresses.
ops-oncall: marking incident as mitigated in #incidents and adding timeline.
